Now let's look at it closely.

'This is simply some kind of real holiday!' This phrase is "some kind of holiday": the ending bit on the second word makes it vague. The first word is the root of the word for the celebration cake. Barinov is very pleased with himself.
Шеф, почему вы так радостно улыбаетесь?

'Chef, why are you smiling so joyfully?' The second word is "you are smiling", polite form, with a ending bit on the end. The first word, "joyfully", comes from The way to express 'joy', the same family as The way to express 'glad'. Lyova is polite and puzzled.

'Everything is turning out even better than our plans.' The second half of this sentence is "better than our plans" with no 'than' is used here: 'plans' is used here just changes its ending. The first phrase, literally "everything folds together", means things are working out.

'Have you already solved the problem with the stove?' The first word of this phrase is "solved", and the same action word also means "decide". The last part is "with the stove": Listen to how 'stove' changes its ending after the connecting Listen to how 'with'. Lyova wants to hear about the stove.
Плита вернётся на кухню вовремя, Лёва.

'The stove will return to the kitchen on time, Lyova.' The first word of this phrase is "will come back", with a self-directed ending bit on the end. The last word, "on time", is written as one word. The middle phrase is "to the kitchen": The speaker uses 'kitchen' changes its ending.
Не говори потом, что я не слушаю.

'Do not say later that I do not listen.' An informal command with a negative little word in front: the first two words mean "don't say". The third word is "later" or "afterwards". Here the action They express 'listen' by in the second half of the sentence means more than hearing: it means heeding what you are told.
Я просто переживаю за вечерний сервис.

'I am simply worried about the evening service.' The first two words of this phrase mean "I'm worried about": this action word takes this connecting word. The third word, "evening", comes from the thing word for evening. The final word is borrowed and easy to catch.
Сегодня вечером наш ресторан заработает состояние.

'Tonight our restaurant will make a fortune.' The fifth word is a action word for earning money, which has When they say 'work' inside it and a starting bit on the front. The last word is a fortune here, though usually it means a state or condition. The first two words, "today in the evening", are how you say "tonight".
Ладно, шеф, я вернусь к работе.

'All right, chef, I will get back to work.' The first word is the easy "all right". The final phrase is "I'll return to work": after the connecting word, Notice the part 'work' changes its ending. Lyova goes back to work.

'Go and supervise the hot kitchen section.' The third and fourth words mean "keep an eye on". The last word means a workshop, and the phrase "hot workshop" is the part of the kitchen where the cooking happens. The first word is "go", to one person.

'I will do everything in the best way, chef.' The last three words of this phrase mean "in the best form", a set expression meaning "perfectly". The first word is "I will do", the future form of the action word. The second word is "everything".

'Now that is the right and cheerful attitude.' The first two words mean "now that's", for pointing something out. The third word is "right", and the fifth word is "cheerful, full of energy". The final word is a mood or attitude. Barinov approves. Now hear it again with fresh ears.
